title: A DNA language model based on multispecies alignment predicts the effects of genome-wide variants

nodes.text: GPN-MSA (genomic pretrained network with multiple-sequence alignment) is a Transformer-based DNA language model that learns nucleotide probability distributions conditioned on both surrounding sequence context and aligned sequences from related species, trained via masked-language modeling on a whole-genome MSA of 100 vertebrate species.
nodes.evidence: GPN-MSA (genomic pretrained network with multiple-sequence alignment), a framework that leverages whole-genome alignments across multiple species... GPN-MSA was trained on a whole-genome MSA of 100 vertebrate species

nodes.text: GPN-MSA is trained with a weighted cross-entropy loss that downweights repetitive elements and upweights conserved elements, with data augmentation that randomly replaces the reference nucleotide in nonconserved regions; the variant effect score is the log-likelihood ratio between the alternate and reference allele.
nodes.evidence: trained with a weighted cross-entropy loss, designed to downweight repetitive elements and upweight conserved elements... The GPN-MSA VEP score is defined as the log-likelihood ratio between the alternate (ALT) and reference (REF) allele

nodes.text: GPN-MSA extends the earlier GPN convolutional model (which worked on unaligned Arabidopsis genomes) to incorporate cross-species alignment, and draws inspiration from the protein MSA Transformer but differs in architecture and training and operates on more complex fragmented whole-genome DNA alignments.
nodes.evidence: It draws inspiration from the MSA Transformer, a protein language model trained on MSAs... there are essential differences in the architecture and training procedure of GPN-MSA from the MSA Transformer

nodes.text: Prior human DNA language models (e.g., Nucleotide Transformer) performed worse than simpler conservation scores at unsupervised variant effect prediction even at large scale, motivating the MSA-based approach.
nodes.evidence: previous attempts at unsupervised VEP with human DNA language models (for example, Nucleotide Transformer) showed inferior performance compared to simpler conservation scores

nodes.text: GPN-MSA trains in only about 3.5 hours on four NVIDIA A100 GPUs, a drastic computational reduction versus models like Nucleotide Transformer (trained 28 days on 128 GPUs).
nodes.evidence: Our model took only 3.5 h to train on four NVIDIA A100 GPUs, which is a considerable reduction... a model trained for 28 days using 128 top-of-the-line graphics processing units

nodes.text: GPN-MSA goes beyond single MSA-column conservation statistics: even at perfectly conserved positions it assigns more deleterious scores to loss-of-function and missense variants than to synonymous variants, leveraging genomic context across multiple columns.
nodes.evidence: even at perfectly conserved positions, GPN-MSA assigns more deleterious scores to loss-of-function... and missense variants compared to synonymous variants

nodes.text: On ClinVar pathogenic versus gnomAD common missense classification, GPN-MSA substantially outperforms other DNA language models (Nucleotide Transformer, HyenaDNA) and also outperforms CADD, phyloP, and the missense-specific ESM-1b.
nodes.evidence: GPN-MSA substantially outperforms other human DNA language models such as Nucleotide Transformer... improved performance compared to genome-wide predictors CADD and phyloP, as well as the missense-specific ESM-1b

nodes.text: On COSMIC frequent versus gnomAD common somatic missense classification and on OMIM regulatory versus gnomAD common variant classification, GPN-MSA achieves the highest performance with substantial margins over other models.
nodes.evidence: GPN-MSA achieves the highest performance, with substantial margins of improvement over other models... GPN-MSA achieves the best performance overall, as well as in each variant category

nodes.text: For rare versus common gnomAD variant enrichment in the deleterious-score tail, GPN-MSA achieves the highest enrichment overall and outperforms SpliceAI on intronic variants and Enformer on nonexonic low-frequency variants.
nodes.evidence: GPN-MSA achieves the highest enrichment overall... it also outperforms SpliceAI, a state-of-the-art splicing predictor... a substantially improved performance over Enformer

nodes.text: On deep mutational scanning data for 31 human proteins, the protein language model ESM-1b achieves the best overall performance, likely benefiting from long-range intra-protein interactions and a larger evolutionary training timescale, while GPN-MSA performs comparably to CADD.
nodes.evidence: the protein language model ESM-1b achieves the best overall performance on this task; it likely benefits from modeling long-range interactions within each protein and training on diverse proteins across a much larger evolutionary timescale

nodes.text: GPN-MSA performs behind CADD on splice-region variants specifically because of difficulty identifying which such variants are not deleterious; precomputed scores are provided for all ~9 billion possible single-nucleotide variants in the human genome.
nodes.evidence: There is one category where GPN-MSA performs behind CADD: splice-region variants... We provide precomputed scores for all ~9 billion possible single-nucleotide variants in the human genome

nodes.text: Only the human reference genome is used to train GPN-MSA, with no human variant dataset used in training, yet the model captures functional attributes such as epigenetic marks and the impact of natural selection.
nodes.evidence: only the reference genome is used to train GPN-MSA and that no human variant dataset is used in training. Nevertheless, GPN-MSA can still capture several functional attributes of variants
